prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
Great question — “shadow work” and “spiritual practice” overlap but are different skill sets, so the best course depends on whether you want Jungian-style shadow integration, trauma‑informed inner work, or foundational meditation/embodiment practices. Below are vetted platforms, specific programs or teachers to look for, and guidance for choosing a course safely.

Top picks by focus

1) Shadow work (Jungian / inner‑psychology oriented)
- Jung Platform — curated workshops and multi‑week courses by Jungian analysts and depth psychologists on shadow integration, dreams, active imagination, persona/shadow work. Good place to find reputable teachers.
- Debbie Ford’s programs (based on The Dark Side of the Light Chasers) — her organization still runs online shadow‑work workshops and guided programs; good for practical exercises in identifying and integrating shadow aspects.
- Udemy/Skillshare — there are several “shadow work” courses for beginners. Quality varies widely; check reviews and instructor background before committing.

2) Trauma‑informed shadow/inner work
- Search for trauma‑informed courses from licensed clinicians (e.g., somatic/EMDR, sensorimotor psych). Institutes like the Sensorimotor Psychotherapy Institute and Somatic Experiencing offer practitioner trainings; some offer public modules or workshops appropriate for non‑clinicians.
- If you have a trauma history, prefer courses that explicitly state a trauma‑informed approach or encourage working with a therapist.

3) Meditation, mindfulness, and foundational spiritual practice
- Palouse Mindfulness MBSR (free, online) — full Mindfulness‑Based Stress Reduction course based on Jon Kabat‑Zinn’s work. Excellent foundation before deep shadow work.
- Sounds True — hosts many courses by Tara Brach, Jack Kornfield, and other well‑known meditation/compassion teachers (good blend of practice and inquiry).
- Insight Timer — thousands of free guided meditations and multi‑week courses (community reviews help identify quality content).
- Coursera — “The Science of Well‑Being” (Yale) and other psychology/meditation courses are useful for building healthy habits and self‑awareness.

4) Broader spiritual/transformational platforms
- The Shift Network — many multi‑week workshops on inner transformation, shadow work, inner child healing, and spiritual practices (instructors vary; check bios).
- Sounds True — large catalog spanning meditation, shadow work, and integrative spiritual practices.
- Gaia — video courses on yoga, energy work, esoteric topics (subscription model).

How to choose the best course
- Clear instructor credentials: prefer licensed clinicians, Jungian analysts, experienced meditation teachers, or established authors.
- Trauma‑informed language: if you have difficult or complex trauma, avoid courses that push rapid catharsis without safety supports.
- Format and support: do you want self‑paced instruction, weekly live calls, community forums, or individual coaching? Look for courses that include community or teacher Q&A if you want support.
- Reviews and sample lessons: watch previews, read reviews, and check refund policies.
- Practical exercises: good shadow work courses include guided journaling prompts, active imagination, role dialogues, and integration practices — not just theory.

Safety and pacing
- Shadow work can trigger intense emotions and memories. If you have a history of complex trauma, bipolar disorder, psychosis, or active suicidal ideation, work with a licensed therapist while doing intense inner work.
- Start with mindfulness, grounding, and self‑compassion practices before intense shadow excavation.
- Allow time for integration: short daily practices, journaling, and supportive community or therapy help turn insights into change.

Recommended reading & free resources to complement courses
- The Dark Side of the Light Chasers — Debbie Ford (popular practical intro)
- Owning Your Own Shadow — Robert A. Johnson (short, clear Jungian intro)
- Meeting the Shadow — edited anthology (classic collection)
- Tara Brach (Free talks & meditations) and Jack Kornfield (teachers with many free resources)
- Insight Timer and YouTube for guided meditations

Suggested pathway (if you’re starting out)
1. Start with a mindfulness course (Palouse MBSR or beginner guided meditations).
2. Read a concise intro book (Johnson or Ford).
3. Take a structured shadow‑work course from Jung Platform or a well‑reviewed program (with journaling prompts and guided exercises).
4. If material becomes intense, pair with counseling/therapy or a trauma‑informed course.

If you want, tell me:
- your experience level (beginner/experienced),
- whether you prefer secular or explicitly spiritual teachers,
- any trauma history,
and I’ll suggest 3–5 specific courses (with links and estimated cost) tailored to you.
